reasons.A: Right period diction ('any one', 'parlour-maid') and some ironic asides, but more short declaratives and a flatter, even-paced argument than the passage's long, piled-up sentences.
reasons.B: Closest movement: long sentences hinged on semicolons and dashes, dry ironic turns ('fewer people will miss the verb'), 'some one'/'any one' spelling; one modern contraction is the main slip.
reasons.C: Modern plain-essay voice: 'everyone'/'anyone', tidy parallel lists, measured hedging and little irony or rhetorical flourish; the rhythm and stance are furthest from the passage.
